title: 1961 AHSME Problem 27
statement: Given two equiangular polygons \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) with different numbers of sides; each angle of \(P_1\) is \(x\) degrees and each angle of \(P_2\) is \(kx\) degrees, where \(k\) is an integer greater than \(1.\) The number of possibilities for the pair \((x,k)\) is:

solutions.text:
Every polygon angle is at least \(60^\circ,\) and every convex polygon angle is less than \(180^\circ.\) Since \(k\ge2\) and \(kx<180^\circ,\) we need \(x<90^\circ.\) The only possible equiangular polygon angle in \([60^\circ,90^\circ)\) is the triangle angle \(x=60^\circ.\) Then \(k=2\) gives \(kx=120^\circ,\) the angle of a regular hexagon; larger \(k\) is impossible. Hence there is one pair.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Use \(kx<180^\circ\) and \(k\ge2\) to constrain the smaller angle \(x\)
